title: Long-lived continuous sensing of multiple clinically useful biomarkers

concept.text: The innovation would be a practical sensor system that repeatedly measures several medically useful molecules during ordinary human activity and remains reliable over a clinically meaningful period. Instead of providing occasional laboratory snapshots, it would show how those molecules change over time. The central challenge is maintaining selective, accurate measurements of several targets together while the device and the surrounding biology change.

Interstitial fluid—the fluid surrounding tissue cells—is one accessible measurement site discussed in the supplied research. The broader concept allows other accessible tissues or fluids, provided their measurements are clinically interpretable. It combines molecular recognition, a stable tissue interface, signal interpretation, and practical device operation. Proposed scope: a usable power source and periodic sensor replacement are acceptable; the system need not operate indefinitely without maintenance.

Measuring multiple molecules is useful only if each measurement remains independently trustworthy and contributes to a defined clinical purpose. The innovation therefore requires more than placing several sensing elements in one device: it must sustain their performance together and establish what their readings mean for care. Sensing supplies information; treatment delivery and replacement of organ function are additional capabilities.

significance.text: Reliable continuous measurements beyond glucose could extend biochemical observation into daily life, revealing changes that occur between appointments or intermittent blood samples. The supplied review describes the rationale for real-time drug monitoring, including adjusting doses to individual needs. A dependable stream of relevant measurements could therefore support better-informed and more timely treatment decisions.

Conditional downstream possibilities include responsive treatment systems that use several molecular signals and care pathways that require fewer burdensome sampling visits. These benefits would depend on choosing actionable biomarkers, understanding their behavior in the sampled fluid, and having effective responses to the information. Continuous measurement alone does not establish that disease can be predicted or prevented, or that acting on the readings improves outcomes.

Continuous glucose monitoring provides an important precedent, but its success cannot simply be generalized to every biomarker. The supplied review identifies a shortage of robust, reusable recognition elements for many targets, particularly proteins measured through affinity binding. Different targets can therefore require different sensing chemistry and validation. The potentially revolutionary advance would be dependable clinical observation across several useful molecules, rather than an assumption that any molecule can be monitored by adapting a glucose sensor.

missing_breakthrough.text: The capability to be established is sustained, selective measurement of several clinically useful biomarkers under real biological and everyday-use conditions. The supplied 2024 review identifies longevity and long-term continuous operation as major challenges at that time. For many targets, recognition elements must remain effective through repeated measurements rather than degrade or become occupied in ways that prevent continued sensing. This is especially difficult for some affinity-based measurements of proteins and other complex targets.

The tissue interface introduces additional barriers. Biofouling, tissue responses, biological interference, and recognition-element degradation can alter the signal over time. Motion can disturb measurements, while physiological delays between blood and interstitial-fluid concentrations complicate interpretation. A system must distinguish meaningful molecular changes from these sources of error and preserve the accuracy of each target throughout use.

Engineering synthesis: useful longevity requires predictable drift, manageable calibration, practical power and data handling, and an acceptable maintenance and replacement burden. These operational requirements come from the candidate’s intended use; the supplied review does not establish power or maintenance as the decisive unresolved scientific barriers. Clinical interpretation is another separate requirement: a technically reliable signal must have a validated relationship to the intended treatment decision.

current_state.text: Zixiong Wu and colleagues’ review, published on 13 March 2024, documents commercial continuous glucose monitoring and research sensors for other molecules in interstitial fluid. It describes commercial glucose sensors operating for more than seven days. That duration is evidence of established glucose-sensing capability within the review’s scope; it does not demonstrate equally durable monitoring of several other clinically useful biomarkers.

The review also describes multiplexed research platforms. One example attributed to Tehrani and colleagues integrates poly(methyl methacrylate)-based glucose, lactate, and alcohol sensors with signal acquisition and wireless transmission in a coin-sized wearable device. The accompanying short human pilot studies support the feasibility of integrated sensing of several molecules, but do not establish the proposed long-lived capability for everyday clinical decision-making. The supplied assessment does not provide a numerical pilot duration or sufficient performance figures to add them here.

Beyond these examples, the review discusses drug monitoring and aptamer-based platforms intended to recognize a range of molecular targets. It identifies limited availability of effective reusable recognition elements and reliable long-term operation as continuing challenges, and calls for further work on targets including cytokines, cortisol, and proteins. These findings establish research breadth and specific barriers as understood in 2024, rather than clinical maturity across all of those targets.

The supplied evidence review reports access to complete saved HTML and a complete 15-page article PDF, with no reported extraction truncation. It did not independently inspect figure images or the cited primary studies, so the examples above remain accounts from a review rather than independently assessed primary results. The separately saved supplementary PDF was identified as a peer-review file, not an additional experimental paper. No freshness search results were supplied, so this material does not establish whether the proposed capability remained unachieved as of 1 November 2026 or whether later work changed the field.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: safely monitor several independently validated, clinically useful biomarkers during everyday human use over a prespecified duration appropriate to a defined clinical application. Specify the target molecules, sampled tissue or fluid, intended users, and treatment decisions before testing. Define acceptable accuracy, drift, calibration frequency, maintenance burden, and replacement frequency. These are proposed criteria for evaluating this innovation, not established consensus thresholds.
completion_criteria.label: Safely monitor several clinically useful biomarkers throughout prespecified everyday use

completion_criteria.text: Proposed analytical validation: compare each target with suitable clinical reference measurements throughout the wear period, including near the end of sensor life. Where the clinical interpretation depends on blood concentrations, establish the relationship between the sampled fluid and blood, including relevant physiological lag. Test simultaneous operation for interference between measurements and evaluate performance under the biological and mechanical disturbances expected in the intended setting.
completion_criteria.label: Validate each biomarker against clinical references throughout sensor life

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical validation: reproduce performance across participants, devices, production batches, and independent testing groups. Report failures, missing data, tissue reactions, calibration interventions, and replacement events alongside successful measurements. Demonstrate that the power source, communications, and maintenance arrangements support the claimed use. Finite studies would establish demonstrated breadth within their tested populations, targets, conditions, and duration; they would not prove universal performance.
completion_criteria.label: Reproduce sensor performance independently and report operational burdens and failures

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical validation: establish accuracy sufficient for the intended treatment decisions and show that using the measurements improves outcomes or materially reduces care burden relative to an appropriate alternative. The study should distinguish the value of additional biochemical information from the benefit of the care decisions made using it. A practical power source and periodic replacement remain acceptable if their burdens are prespecified and compatible with the intended application.
completion_criteria.label: Measurements improve outcomes or materially reduce care burden

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison: BME-16, “Long-lived tissue-integrated interfaces for implants,” overlaps directly with the need to control tissue responses and maintain a stable sensing interface. Its scope is broader than molecular measurement. BME-18 additionally requires selective recognition chemistry, simultaneous measurement of several targets, and clinical interpretation.

Roster-based comparison: BME-13, “Durable autonomous artificial-organ replacement,” could use continuous biomarker measurements as inputs to an autonomous system. Its defining goal is replacement of organ function, whereas BME-18 concerns obtaining reliable measurements. BME-05, “Programmable living medicines that sense and respond inside the body,” likewise combines sensing with a therapeutic response and uses a different implementation approach. Neither capability follows automatically from successful biomarker monitoring.

Roster-based comparison: BME-07, “A broadly effective early-warning test for lethal cancers,” shares the need for clinically validated biomarkers, but has a disease-detection objective. Continuous access to molecular signals would not by itself establish early cancer detection. BME-15, “Accessible deep-body molecular imaging,” overlaps in observing molecular biology, while emphasizing spatial information inside the body; BME-18 emphasizes repeated measurements over time at accessible sampling sites.

Roster-based comparison: BME-10, “Validated patient-specific models for testing treatments before use,” could draw on longitudinal biomarker data to characterize a patient or assess a model’s predictions. Reliable measurements would be useful inputs, but would not themselves validate a model or establish its ability to predict treatment effects. These relationships preserve the separate goals of sensing, modeling, diagnosis, and intervention.

unresolved_issues: The supplied material does not establish advances after the March 2024 review or whether the complete proposed capability had been achieved by 1 November 2026.
The target biomarker panel, intended clinical application, required duration, accuracy limits, and acceptable maintenance burden remain to be selected and justified.
The cited multiplexed human pilots were not independently assessed through their primary papers; their numerical duration and detailed performance are not supplied here.
Clinical outcome improvement or reduced care burden from the proposed long-lived multiplexed system remains to be demonstrated.
Related-concept comparisons rely on the supplied roster titles; detailed specifications would be needed to resolve finer scope boundaries.

brief.title: Lasting monitoring of several body chemicals
possible: Patients and clinicians could follow several medically useful molecules throughout daily life, seeing changes that occasional blood tests miss. A dependable sensor could keep those measurements useful for long enough to guide a defined course of care.
why: For people whose treatment depends on changing body chemistry, these readings could help clinicians adjust medicines to individual needs and respond sooner. They could also reduce burdensome sampling visits.

sources.showed: Their review describes established blood-sugar monitoring and experimental sensors for other molecules in the fluid surrounding tissue cells. It identifies lasting accuracy and reusable molecule-recognition chemistry as continuing challenges.
sources.cited_for: The review explains why success with blood sugar does not automatically extend to other molecules.
sources.not_established: It does not demonstrate a lasting system that measures several useful molecules accurately enough to guide care.

sources.showed: An implanted light-based sensor measured several molecules in a small human study lasting 28 days. The authors reported accurate readings and good tolerance; one device lost communication.
sources.quote: The implanted YANG sensor was safe and well tolerated and did not cause any infectious or wound healing complications.
sources.cited_for: The study supports the feasibility of measuring several molecules with an implant over an extended period.
sources.not_established: The small feasibility study does not establish dependable everyday use across populations or improved care.

sources.showed: A small human study tested a single probe measuring blood sugar and lactate, a byproduct of metabolism. Comparisons with blood tests supported feasibility, with further accuracy improvements needed.
sources.quote: Our initial data support safety and functionality of a novel glucose/lactate continuous multi-analyte sensor.
sources.cited_for: The study supports measuring different molecules through a shared probe and comparing readings with clinical references.
sources.not_established: The brief study does not establish lasting accuracy, reliable insertion or independent reproduction.

sources.showed: They built a wireless ring that measures several chemicals in sweat during daily activities. It supported about 12 hours of continuous monitoring.
sources.quote: The simultaneous biomarker monitoring was validated under diverse daily settings.
sources.cited_for: The ring demonstrates integrated chemical sensing, power and wireless communication during daily use.
sources.not_established: It does not establish sustained clinical reliability or treatment benefits from its sweat measurements.

sources.showed: They built a flexible wristband combining tiny needles for chemical sensing with measurements of blood pressure and heart activity. Human tests tracked responses to meals, alcohol and exercise.
sources.quote:
The multimodal platform offers continuous glucose, lactate and alcohol
monitoring, along with simultaneous ultrasonic measurements of blood
pressure, arterial stiffness and heart rate
sources.cited_for: The wristband demonstrates simultaneous chemical and physical measurements during common activities.
sources.not_established: It does not establish lasting performance or better treatment outcomes.

shown: De Ridder and colleagues demonstrated an implanted sensor for several molecules over 28 days in a small human study. Other teams have demonstrated wearable probes, rings and wristbands. Together, these results show working combinations of sensors, while leaving sustained clinical usefulness to be demonstrated.
missing: Each molecule still needs to be measured reliably throughout everyday use despite motion, tissue reactions and changes in the sensor.
Each reading needs a validated relationship to the clinical decision it would inform, including any delay relative to blood levels.
Independent studies need to reproduce performance and establish acceptable failures, upkeep and replacement burdens.
Trials need to show that using the measurements improves outcomes or materially reduces care burden.

milestones.label: Safe monitoring throughout a defined period of daily use
milestones.explanation: A human study would have to safely track several independently validated, useful molecules throughout a predefined period of everyday use. This would establish that the combined system meets its intended clinical purpose.

milestones.label: Every measurement stays accurate throughout sensor life
milestones.explanation: Each molecule would have to match suitable clinical reference tests throughout use, accounting for blood relationships, delays and interference. This would make each reading independently trustworthy.

milestones.label: Independent studies reproduce performance and reveal practical burdens
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce performance across people, devices and production batches while reporting failures and upkeep. This would establish how reliably the system works beyond an initial demonstration.

milestones.label: Using the readings improves care
milestones.explanation: A clinical study would have to show that sufficiently accurate readings improve outcomes or materially reduce care burden against an appropriate alternative. This would establish the value of acting on the additional information.

uncertain: The best combination of molecules, clinical purpose and required monitoring duration remains to be justified.
Acceptable accuracy, adjustment frequency and replacement burden depend on the intended use.
It remains unclear how broadly success with simpler molecules will extend to proteins and other complex targets.

page.title: Continuous multi-analyte monitoring
page.definition: A body-worn or implanted sensor measures two or more molecular biomarkers throughout a clinically validated wear period. The authorized glucose–ketone implementation measures glucose and beta-hydroxybutyrate, a ketone, in interstitial fluid—the fluid between tissue cells—every minute for up to 10 days.

goal.need: Glucose does not fully indicate ketone status. Records from September 2014 to September 2024 show ketone elevations below the glucose threshold commonly used to trigger spot ketone testing. Measuring both molecules addresses this information gap; the observational study does not establish that continuous monitoring prevents diabetic ketoacidosis.

completion.title: FDA authorizes continuous glucose–ketone monitoring for a 10-day wear period.
completion.criterion: FDA grants marketing authorization for a single sensor to monitor both glucose and beta-hydroxybutyrate continuously for diabetes management over its labeled 10-day wear period, with glucose outputs usable for treatment decisions and ketone outputs interpreted alongside glucose, symptoms and other relevant factors. This test was met by Libre Duo 10 Day on 25 August 2026; the corrected classification order is dated 26 August 2026.
completion.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, De Novo request DEN250049 and its corrected classification order.
completion.threshold_quote: As a result of this order, you may immediately market your device as described in the De Novo request, subject to the general control provisions of the FD&C Act and the special controls identified in this order.
completion.basis: Marketing authorization supplies an external clinical-use test with a defined analyte pair, intended population and wear period. Achievement applies to this glucose–ketone system; it does not validate other biomarker panels or demonstrate that monitoring reduces hospital admissions.

milestones.title: A multi-analyte sensor passes nonclinical function and safety checks supporting first human use.
milestones.criterion: Before human use, nonclinical evidence supports intended sensing function and addresses device-specific safety, including sterility, biocompatibility, software, electromagnetic and chemical compatibility, and catastrophic failure modes. Hoss et al. reported a laboratory component demonstration in 32 dual glucose–ketone sensors: glucose 0–30 mmol/L, ketones 0–10 mmol/L, ketone correlation r > 0.99 and 10–90% response time <5 minutes. These results address analytical function; they do not establish the complete preclinical safety assessment.
milestones.set_by: FDA, 2013 early-feasibility guidance, sections 6 and 6.3.1. This is nonbinding, general medical-device guidance with device-specific acceptance criteria.
milestones.threshold_quote: In general, for an early feasibility study, the evaluation strategy should be focused on identifying the information needed to address significant safety concerns and support basic device functionality.

milestones.title: A multi-analyte sensor demonstrates proof of principle and initial clinical safety in people.
milestones.criterion: An ethics-approved early feasibility study demonstrates proof of principle and initial clinical safety. GLOW, conducted from 25 February 2021 to 19 July 2021, tested YANG implants in seven people: four with type 1 diabetes and three healthy volunteers. Implantation lasted 28 days, with six 8-hour measurement visits. Six devices remained operational; one lost communication. No infection or wound-healing complications occurred. Glucose, ketone, lactate and ethanol estimates used exploratory cross-validation, with models trained at the start of each measurement visit.
milestones.set_by: FDA, 2013 early-feasibility guidance, defining a general medical-device development stage. GLOW received ethics approval from Antwerp University Hospital.
milestones.threshold_quote: Early feasibility studies allow for early clinical evaluation of devices to provide proof of principle and initial clinical safety data.

milestones.title: A glucose–ketone sensor produces zero FDA-defined extreme glucose or ketone classification errors.
milestones.criterion: In clinical comparisons, no sensor glucose value <70 mg/dL may correspond to blood glucose >180 mg/dL, and none >180 mg/dL may correspond to blood glucose <70 mg/dL. No sensor ketone value <0.6 mmol/L may correspond to blood ketones >3.0 mmol/L, and none >3.0 mmol/L may correspond to blood ketones <0.6 mmol/L. These are four specified extreme-error exclusions, not the complete FDA accuracy requirements.
milestones.set_by: FDA, DEN250049 special controls (1)(v)(H–I) and (1)(vi)(B–C), written specifically for integrated continuous glucose–ketone monitoring systems.
milestones.threshold_quote: When iCGK ketone sensor values are less than 0.6 mmol/L, no corresponding blood ketone value shall be above 3.0 mmol/L.

milestones.title: A glucose–ketone sensor maintains clinical performance throughout its claimed wear period.
milestones.criterion: Clinical studies compare each analyte with parallel blood specimens measured by FDA-accepted laboratory methods, cover the measuring range and intended population, and demonstrate consistent performance throughout sensor life without clinically significant data gaps. FDA reported six studies enrolling more than 600 people aged 2 years or older for Libre Duo 10 Day, supporting ketone performance across 10 days. This is a regulatory summary, not a peer-reviewed report of those six studies.
milestones.set_by: FDA, DEN250049 special controls (1)(i–iv) and (1)(viii), written specifically for integrated continuous glucose–ketone monitoring systems.
milestones.threshold_quote: Clinical study results must demonstrate consistent analytical and clinical performance throughout the sensor wear period.

not_found: A public FDA decision summary giving individual sample sizes and analyte-specific results for the six Libre Duo studies could not be opened.
The accessible ClinicalTrials.gov GLOW page did not expose its registered endpoints.

results.finding: GLOW tested the YANG multi-analyte implant in 7 participants and found no infections or wound-healing complications.
results.detail: The ethics-approved feasibility study used exploratory, visit-trained models; one sensor lost communication.
results.quote: The implanted YANG sensor was safe and well tolerated and did not cause any infectious or wound healing complications. Six out 7 sensors remained fully operational over the entire study period.

results.finding: In GLOW, 6 of 7 YANG implants produced measurements across the 28-day implantation period.
results.detail: The sensor was active only during measurement visits, with exploratory models trained at each visit. One device lost communication; ketones were compared with blood test strips.
results.quote: Six out of seven implanted devices transmitted good quality NIR spectra that allowed to measure glucose, ketones, ethanol, and lactate with excellent accuracy during the full implantation period.

results.finding: Glucose–lactate sensors passed biocompatibility testing and achieved a sterility assurance level of 10−6; sample size not reported.
results.detail: The paper does not report the complete nonclinical assessment, including software, electromagnetic and chemical compatibility, or catastrophic failure modes.
results.quote:
The sensors were determined to be safe for implantation after successfully passing biocompatibility testing, in accordance with ISO 10993, as well as having a sterility assurance level of 10
−6
, in accordance with ISO 11137-2.

results.finding: In a first-in-human glucose–lactate sensor study, 16 adults participated and no adverse events were recorded.
results.detail: The ethics-approved four-day feasibility study analyzed paired sensor and blood data from 11 participants. Three insertions failed and two participants trialed an alternate sensor design; calibration was retrospective.
results.quote: No adverse events were recorded throughout the study.

results.finding: CHARM’s multi-analyte sensors showed concentration-dependent responses in vitro across 3 measurements.
results.detail: The laboratory tests support analytical function, but the text does not establish the complete device-specific preclinical safety assessment or its timing before human use.

results.finding: CHARM tracked glucose and ketone dynamics in one person with type 1 diabetes over approximately 10 hours.
results.detail: The study demonstrates human proof of principle, but the supplied text does not report ethics approval or an initial clinical safety assessment.
results.quote: Plots highlighting glucose and ketone dynamics, validated against blood and commercial CGM readings over a ~ 10-hour study with i) multiple meals and one ketone drink, and ii) one meal with two ketone drinks.

results.finding: CHARM’s 420 paired glucose data points fell in consensus error grid zones A and B.
results.detail: The study also compared ketones with commercial blood meters, but did not establish performance across the full measuring range and intended population with FDA-accepted laboratory methods throughout the claimed wear period.

results.detail: Nonclinical mechanical testing addresses device function, but the paper does not report the complete preclinical safety assessment required by the criterion.

results.finding: BLUE monitored multiple biomarkers in healthy participants for up to 400 minutes; sample size not stated.
results.detail: The on-body trials demonstrate initial sensing feasibility, but the supplied text does not establish ethics approval or report clinical safety outcomes sufficient to satisfy the criterion.

activities for 220 and 400 min to assess and understand the body’s
response during different daily stimulations.

results.finding: In a pig study, 6 of 9 implanted glucose–oxygen barcode sensors were recovered after 7 months.
results.detail: The recovered sensors were externally readable. The paper also reports laboratory sensing, sterilization effects and tissue responses, but does not establish the complete device-specific safety assessment needed to support first human use.

results.finding: SHINE implantable sensor study, sample size not stated: zero device-related serious adverse events reported.
results.detail: The company reports technical feasibility and participant feedback, but does not state the sample size, ethics approval, or quantitative evidence that the sensor measured multiple metabolites.
results.quote: A strong safety profile with no device-related serious adverse events

results.finding: Libre Duo 10 Day: more than 600 participants; ketone performance was demonstrated across 10 days.
results.detail: The FDA reports accuracy evaluation for both analytes across a range of levels, but describes performance throughout wear only for ketones. The release does not specify blood comparison methods or clinically significant data gaps.
results.quote: The results demonstrated that the device accurately tracked clinically meaningful differences in ketone levels across its 10-day wear period, including identifying elevated ketone levels before the onset of diabetic ketoacidosis.

results.finding: Libre DUO 10 Day: 68.8% of pediatric sensors lasted the full 10 days; sample size not stated.
results.detail: In adults, 84.1% of sensors lasted the full 10 days. The study reports sensor wear duration but does not establish analyte accuracy against parallel blood specimens or consistent clinical performance throughout wear.
results.quote: A study was conducted to evaluate the Libre DUO 10 Day sensor wear duration. Results showed that 84.1% of sensors in the adult population and 68.8% of sensors in the pediatric population lasted the full 10 days.
